JAMES L. CLARK

STUDIO

949 HOME STREET, BRONX

NEW YORK CITY

# 5/30|14

May 22nd, 1914.

Col. Theodore Roosevelt,

Oyster Bay,

New York.

My dear Col. Roosevelt:

Regarding the three lion ruge which were

returned to me for repairing:

I am enclosing you several photographs of

lion head which I have mounted for the wall and with which I have been very successful; several men having sent me their lion rugs to put into this shape.

I offer these ag

a suggestion for the ruge that you have returned, since, after two attempts, it seems impossible to find any way to keep your lion ruge from wrinkling; as I have said before, this is due to the original tanning.

In mounting these heade for the wall the

body skin is not cut away, but tucked inside the head and shoulders .

The mounts are

much more satisfactory in appear-

ance than the rugs inasmuch as they are more natural, and the main difference is that the skin gets now ware such as it is subject to on the floor.

I would strongly advise that your rugs be

made into similar mounts, and would be very glad to hear from you regarding this.

I am under the impression that there ie

something to be fixed on the elephant tusk gong;

if this

13 80, I would be glad to fix it whenever you so desire.

With congratulations for you recent success-

full trip and with kindeet regarde, I am

Very respectfull:
